propositions: HTTP 429 responses with Retry-After headers are not retried by the DC transport, causing hard failures when rate-limited despite server guidance
Read operations must distinguish themselves from mutations to enable safe retry logic, as retrying mutations after 429 risks duplicate writes when the server began processing before responding

The Retry-After header and jitter logic must be reused from _errors module and applied consistently across two distinct call paths: _paged_search via _call_logged (PATH A) and direct get_comment_map per-issue fetches (PATH B)

Per-call opt-in with default-OFF is required to prevent future mutations from inheriting 429 retry by omission, necessitating edits to both _call_logged to forward the flag and four specific read call sites to pass True
Capability must degrade gracefully when Retry-After is absent, matching pre-8.6 and Server behavior where rate limiting is unsupported or disabled

The delay arithmetic must apply jitter after parsing Retry-After (up to 20% per Atlassian prescription) then clamp to MAX_BACKOFF_S, differing deliberately from the ADR-0036 connectivity backoff which jitters only its curve
